summary.en: Express capabilities with interfaces, resolve defaults and preview single-method contracts.
summary.bn: ইন্টারফেস দিয়ে সক্ষমতা প্রকাশ করো, default মেথডের দ্বন্দ্ব মেটাও এবং এক-মেথডের চুক্তি চেনো।

notes: Default and static interface methods: Java 8. Private interface helpers: Java 9.

sections.title: Describe a capability without choosing a family
Several views can reach one implementation
Use contracts, defaults and explicit conflict resolution
A default supplies behaviour, not instance storage
Choose the kind of shared structure you need
Check visibility and ownership of each method
Interface bodies have explicit release boundaries
Promise the capability the caller needs

examples.title: One device, two capabilities
examples.explanationHtml: Terminal implements both capabilities. Its implementations are public because the interface methods are public.

examples.title: Default behaviour and a static utility
examples.explanationHtml: ExamNotice inherits text(). valid() belongs to Notice and is called through the interface name.

examples.title: Resolve competing defaults
examples.explanationHtml: Unrelated Left and Right defaults conflict. Joint overrides name() and explicitly combines both direct interface implementations.

examples.title: A single-method policy without lambda syntax
examples.explanationHtml: FeePolicy has one abstract operation and can later be implemented by a lambda. The named class keeps the contract visible here.

practice.title: Two counters, one contract
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..20) then n integers (0..100). Implement Counter in EvenCounter and PositiveCounter. Print the even count and positive count on separate lines; zero is even but not positive.

practice.title: Price policy
practice.statementHtml: Read kind (0 full, 1 half) and price (0..10000). Implement PricePolicy in FullPrice and HalfPrice. Print apply(price); half price uses integer division.
hints: Use the interface type for the selected policy.

practice.title: Split capabilities
practice.statementHtml: A scanner-only device is forced to implement print() and scan(). Redesign its interfaces.
practice.answerHtml: Define separate Printer and ScannerDevice interfaces. A scan-only class implements ScannerDevice. A combined machine implements both. Callers depend on the capability they actually need, so scan-only devices need no fake print operation.

practice.title: Resolve default ambiguity
practice.statementHtml: A and B declare unrelated default String label(). C implements both. Give a valid label() fragment choosing A.
practice.answerHtml:
@Override
public String label() {
    return A.super.label();
}

C explicitly resolves the conflict. A must be a direct superinterface eligible for this qualified super call.
hints: Override once and name the desired direct interface.

quiz.prompt: What does the inherited interface default return?
quiz.explanation: No class override is present, so the interface default supplies Hello.

quiz.prompt: Which competing defaults does Both.combine() use?
quiz.explanation: The explicit calls request B then A.

quiz.prompt: What happens when a class implementation meets an interface default?
quiz.explanation: The inherited public class implementation takes precedence over the interface default.

quiz.prompt: How many direct interfaces may one class implement?
quiz.explanation: A class can extend one class and implement several interfaces.
options: None if it extends a class

quiz.prompt: What access does void run(); have in an interface?
quiz.explanation: An ordinary abstract interface operation is public, so implementations cannot narrow it.

quiz.prompt: How should a static interface method valid() on Rule be called?
quiz.explanation: Static interface methods belong to their declaring interface and are not inherited as class methods.

quiz.prompt: What does a functional interface require?
quiz.explanation: Default and static methods do not count toward the single abstract method requirement.
options: Only one method of any kind

quiz.prompt: Which shared-state need usually favours an abstract class?
quiz.explanation: An abstract class can own instance fields and initialize them through constructors.

quiz.prompt: What are ordinary interface fields implicitly?
quiz.explanation: Interface fields represent shared constants rather than per-object mutable state.

quiz.prompt: Which release introduced interface default and static methods?
quiz.explanation: Java 8 added these methods; private interface helpers arrived later in Java 9.

keyPoints.en: Interfaces name capabilities shared by unrelated implementations.
keyPoints.bn: সম্পর্কহীন ক্লাসেও একই সক্ষমতার জন্য ইন্টারফেস ব্যবহার করা যায়।

keyPoints.en: Interface abstract methods require public implementations.
keyPoints.bn: ইন্টারফেসের অ্যাবস্ট্রাক্ট মেথড public হিসেবে বাস্তবায়ন করতে হয়।

keyPoints.en: Conflicting unrelated defaults need an explicit override.
keyPoints.bn: সম্পর্কহীন default মেথডের দ্বন্দ্ব ওভাররাইড করে মেটাতে হয়।

keyPoints.en: Static interface helpers belong to the declaring interface.
keyPoints.bn: স্ট্যাটিক হেল্পার যে ইন্টারফেসে লেখা হয় সেটিরই মেথড।

keyPoints.en: One abstract contract makes an interface functional.
keyPoints.bn: একটি অ্যাবস্ট্রাক্ট চুক্তি থাকলে ইন্টারফেস ফাংশনাল হয়।

examQuestions.question: Compare an abstract class with an interface for a payment capability.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
NeedAbstract classInterface
Instance stateSupportedNo instance fields
ConstructionConstructorsNo constructors
Multiple contractsOne class superclassMany implemented interfaces

A payment capability usually fits an interface. A tightly related family sharing validated state may also use an abstract base.

examQuestions.question: Explain why implementing two defaults does not automatically combine them.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Unrelated defaults with the same signature are ambiguous. The implementing class must override the method. It can select one direct interface’s default or combine both explicitly. Java does not infer the intended policy.

examQuestions.question: Design a functional Discount interface and explain the role of its annotation.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
@FunctionalInterface
interface Discount {
    int reduce(int price);
}

The annotation checks the single abstract method condition. It does not require a lambda; a named class may implement reduce.
